pos.personaBrief: Ajax held 61% in the 1995 final and used possession as a control and defensive tool (StatsBomb), patient and ball-oriented per Ballverliebt.

pro.personaBrief: Systemised build-up from the goalkeeper with set patterns and rotation, waiting patiently for the opponent's error (StatsBomb, FourFourTwo, Ballverliebt).

est.personaBrief: Roles tied strictly to the position, not the player, and moves in set patterns; a sacred system (Ballverliebt, Bergkamp, FourFourTwo).

lar.personaBrief: Wingers held the width and were the ones to reach the byline and cross, while full-backs only switched play; diamond midfield central column (Ballverliebt, StatsBomb, FourFourTwo).

blo.personaBrief: Collective hounding to win the ball back quickly and compact pack pressing (FourFourTwo, Ajax Daily), not a low block.

mar.personaBrief: Mixed: libero Blind with Reiziger and F. de Boer as classic man-markers against the ball (Ballverliebt), Davids tracking wide men; a rehearsed corner routine uses blocking.

pla.personaBrief: Own system imposed on all, played whatever the opponent, with only small tweaks at half-time (Rijkaard dropped five yards); Van Gaal 'won't budge'.

res.personaBrief: Dominant, proactive approach: Milan and Ajax play to win, unlike teams that avoid defeat (Van Gaal 1995); winning through the method rather than defensive closing.

sis.personaBrief: The system was everything and the individual subordinated himself (Ballverliebt); sacred system, collectief, disciplined basic tasks.

jog.personaBrief: Multi-functional, technically and tactically intelligent players, passing drills at speed; physical strength valued but not decisive.

bas.personaBrief: Academy-based team: six of the starting XI in the 1995 final were graduates, a youth scheme over star recruiting, with Kluivert and Kanu at 18 (StatsBomb, These Football Times).

lid.personaBrief: Disciplinarian, dictator-like image, relentless rehearsal, 'won't budge', demanded discipline from everyone (FourFourTwo, Frank de Boer).
